source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue routine observation until the client makes an actual exit attempt, because questions about doors alone do not justify activating elopement precautions.","B":"Initiate the unit's elopement precautions based on the risk assessment, such as enhanced observation and appropriate control of access points and exits.","C":"Move the client closer to the nurses' station but leave the usual observation level unchanged, because location alone is sufficient to manage the identified risk.","D":"Document the elopement concern and ask family to reinforce staying on the unit, but defer environmental precautions unless the client reaches an exit."}}
source_row.rationale: AHRQ PSNet recommends assessment and preventive precautions for patients at elopement risk, including enhanced observation and environmental controls appropriate to the setting. Option B applies those measures after the concerning behavior is identified. Option A waits for an actual attempt before acting. Option C changes location but leaves the observation plan unchanged. Option D relies on documentation and family reinforcement while deferring precautions that address the identified safety risk.
source_row.source_detail: AHRQ PSNet — Elopement: identify elopement risk and implement preventive precautions appropriate to the setting, including observation protocols and environmental/access controls in behavioral-health settings. Current AHRQ PSNet elopement patient-safety guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15 against recent PSNet-indexed elopement literature. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: asepsis, equipment/environmental safety, incident/event prevention and infection-control activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: An inpatient psychiatric client repeatedly asks about exit locations and how visitor badges open doors. Which nursing action best addresses the identified elopement risk?
